LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 1.1.1 PRONUNCIATION AND VOCABULARY

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: THE FAMILY SUGGESTED VOCABULARY: family, relative, care-giver, sibling, orphan, 
Topic 1.1: Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary, part of THE FAMILY SUGGESTED VOCABULARY: family, relative, care-giver, sibling, orphan,  in Grade 4 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: Why should we pronounce sounds and words correctly?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. pronounce sounds and words correctly for effective oral communication,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. use vocabulary in sentences for effective oral communication,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. listen attentively to an oral text for comprehension,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. appreciate the importance of accurate pronunciation in oral texts.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. pronounce sounds and words correctly for effective oral communication,

   Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. use vocabulary in sentences for effective oral communication,

   Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. listen attentively to an oral text for comprehension,

   Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. appreciate the importance of accurate pronunciation in oral texts.

   Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. say tongue twisters with words containing the sounds; /t/ /d/ /f/ /v/ and the digraph /tw/,

2. repeat saying minimal pairs with the sounds /t/ /d/ /f/ /v/ and the digraph /tw/ from the teacher or an audio recording,

3. find out the correct pronunciation of words and sentences from electronic or print dictionaries,

4. match words that have the same sounds and use them to construct sentences collaboratively,

5. work jointly to search for words related to the theme on the internet and use them in sentences,

6. listen to an audio text and answer

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. say tongue twisters with words containing the sounds; /t/ /d/ /f/ /v/ and the digraph /tw/,
2. repeat saying minimal pairs with the sounds /t/ /d/ /f/ /v/ and the digraph /tw/ from the teacher or an audio recording,
3. find out the correct pronunciation of words and sentences from electronic or print dictionaries,
4. match words that have the same sounds and use them to construct sentences collaboratively,
5. work jointly to search for words related to the theme on the internet and use them in sentences,
6. listen to an audio text and answer

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: This is enhanced as the learner pronounces words correctly and accurately with

others.

• Digital Literacy: It is enhanced as the learner uses digital devices to listen to sounds and search for correct pronunciation

of words.

Values:
• Unity: This is developed as the learner works collaboratively during group tasks such as playing a language game.

• Respect: This is enhanced as the learner appreciates individual differences in pronunciation and articulation of sounds.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Social Cohesion: This is promoted as learners interact with texts on the theme of family to get the vocabulary.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner is able to connect the concept of correct pronunciation and articulation to their learning in Kiswahili and

Indigenous languages.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. pronounce sounds and words correctly for effective oral communication,
2. use vocabulary in sentences for effective oral communication,
3. listen attentively to an oral text for comprehension,
4. appreciate the importance of accurate pronunciation in oral texts.

Remember the key question: Why should we pronounce sounds and words correctly?
